title: Jesus, with All Thy Saints Above
description: Jesus, with All Thy Saints Above in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 29, headed “Redemption by price and power”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Je-sus, with all thy saints a-bove My tongue would bear her part, Would sound a-loud thy sa-ving love, And sing thy bleed-ing heart.

lines: Jesus, with all thy saints above
My tongue would bear her part,
Would sound aloud thy saving love,
Bless'd be the Lamb, my dearest Lord,
Who bought me with his blood,
And quench'd his Father's flaming sword
The Lamb that freed my captive soul
And sent the lion down to howl
All glory to the dying Lamb,
While angels live to know his Name,
Or saints to feel his grace.

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
